overview: A high, dry desert of monasteries, blue lakes and huge skies. Leh is at 3,500 m; Pangong and Nubra need long drives over high passes.
fit: Better when the younger one is about 7 or older. Altitude sickness is a real risk for small children.
season: June–September is the season (15–25°C days, cold nights). Roads to Leh by land open May–October. Winter is extremely cold.
gettingAround: Hire a local taxi (outside taxis aren't allowed for sightseeing).

todo.title: Thiksey and Hemis monasteries
todo.why: Big monasteries with festivals in summer

todo.title: Nubra Valley: Bactrian camel ride
todo.book: Crosses Khardung La; check altitude tolerance

foodTips: Indian vegetarian food is widely available in Leh.
save: Stay in Leh and do day trips if the kids struggle with altitude
Fly in early in the season for lower fares
safety: Acute mountain sickness can be serious for young children; consult your paediatrician first
Carry oxygen cans in the cab
Inner Line Permit needed for Nubra and Pangong
health: Diamox only on a doctor's advice
Drink lots of water; no exertion on day 1–2
kids: Seriously consider waiting until the younger one is 7+

Magnetic Hill, Sangam, Hall of Fame
Nubra Valley overnight (if all are well)
